content.title: About
content.content: Paneer is a fresh Indian cheese made from whole milk (usually cow or buffalo) without the use of bacterial cultures. The milk is heated to a boil and an acid (lemon juice, vinegar, or yogurt) is added, causing the proteins to coagulate into a curd that is drained and pressed into blocks. Paneer has a soft, slightly grainy texture and a neutral flavor, allowing it to absorb the spices and sauces it is cooked with.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Paneer is not fermented and does not age like many other cheeses.
Unlike most cheeses, paneer is made without rennet, making it suitable for vegetarians.
Traditionally, paneer is cut into cubes and fried or added to curries, sauces, and salads.
Paneer is a staple source of protein for vegetarians in Indian cuisine.
There are several varieties: soft paneer for fresh use and firmer paneer for grilling and frying.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Paneer provides about 18 g of protein per 100 g, making it a valuable source of animal protein for vegetarians.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium in paneer supports bone and dental health, especially important for those on plant‑based diets.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: During cooking, much of the lactose is removed, so paneer is often tolerated by people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Paneer supplies vitamin B12, a nutrient typically found in animal products that is essential for nerve function.

items.title: Supports muscle maintenance
items.content: The combination of protein and calcium helps with muscle repair after exercise.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to casein or whey proteins present in paneer.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: When salt is added during preparation, paneer can become a source of excess sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Paneer is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Using low‑quality milk can introduce pathogens; purchase paneer from reputable producers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Paneer can be eaten fresh, added to salads, cooked in sauces and curries, grilled, or pan‑fried until golden. Its neutral taste makes it ideal for marinating with herbs, spices, and aromatics.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store paneer in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized pieces; thaw in the fridge before use.
